skill.name: when-gathering-requirements-use-interactive-planner
skill.description: Guide requirements gathering with structured interactive questions, follow-up prompts, validation steps, and final specification planning.
skill.summary: Gather requirements through a structured interactive planning workflow.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive caused by a Markdown YAML code fence in SKILL.md, not executable Ruby or shell syntax. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, network access, or malicious intent was found in the reviewed skill content.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 8 starts a Markdown YAML code fence that documents skill metadata. It is not Ruby backtick execution and does not invoke shell commands.

content.value_statement: Teams often start projects with unclear goals, missing constraints, and weak acceptance criteria. This skill structures discovery questions into validated requirements, specifications, and action plans.
actual_capabilities: Guides initial discovery with structured interactive questions.
Organizes follow-up questions around goals, scope, priorities, timelines, and constraints.
Transforms responses into requirements, specifications, validation notes, and action plans.
Defines a five-phase workflow from discovery through final documentation.
Provides quick-start, detailed process, and visual workflow references.
limitations: Does not implement the AskUserQuestion tool itself.
Depends on clear user responses and stakeholder availability.
Does not verify requirements against live systems or external sources.
Provides process guidance, not automated project management execution.

use_cases.title: Scope a New Feature
use_cases.description: Guide product discovery before implementation by collecting goals, affected components, priorities, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Prepare Technical Specifications
use_cases.description: Turn stakeholder answers into structured functional requirements, non-functional requirements, risks, and milestones.

use_cases.title: Validate Project Readiness
use_cases.description: Review gathered requirements with stakeholders and identify gaps before work begins.

prompt_templates.title: Start Discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the interactive planner to gather requirements for this project. Start with goals, scope, affected users, and expected outcome.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify Technical Needs
prompt_templates.scenario: Add more detail after initial discovery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Ask follow-up questions about technical requirements, constraints, scale, integrations, timeline, risks, and priority tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Specification
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert responses into a usable planning document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize the collected answers into functional requirements, non-functional requirements, acceptance criteria, risks, milestones, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Finalize
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the requirements for missing decisions, unclear ownership, unresolved risks, and approval needs. Then create a final action plan.

output_examples.input: A team wants to define requirements for a customer dashboard.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks about target users, dashboard metrics, permissions, refresh frequency, launch timeline, and success criteria.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead has stakeholder answers but no specification.
output_examples.output: The assistant organizes the answers into requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, risks, milestones, and remaining questions.

output_examples.input: A project coordinator needs stakeholder approval before development starts.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares a validation checklist, highlights gaps, and produces an action plan for final approval.

best_practices: Ask short questions that separate goals, scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria.
Use multi-select options for priorities, affected components, and stakeholder preferences.
Validate the final specification with stakeholders before creating the action plan.
anti_patterns: Do not skip follow-up questions when answers are vague or incomplete.
Do not treat initial stakeholder preferences as approved requirements.
Do not create implementation tasks before documenting risks and acceptance criteria.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps gather, clarify, validate, and document project requirements through a structured interactive planning process.

faq.question: Does it work outside Claude Code?
faq.answer: The workflow can guide Claude and Codex sessions, but the original process references Claude Code interactive questions.

faq.question: Does it create final specifications?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides the assistant to organize answers into specifications, acceptance criteria, risks, and action plans.

faq.question: Can it replace stakeholder approval?
faq.answer: No. It supports stakeholder validation, but people still need to review and approve the requirements.

faq.question: Is it only for software projects?
faq.answer: No. It fits software projects best, but the discovery and validation process can support broader planning work.

faq.question: Does it run commands or access external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is process documentation and does not require command execution or network access.
